feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: it shows clear progression, relevant public-sector scope, and solid technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce punch.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope and responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” which strengthen impact and credibility.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, experience, and technical stack; the profile is coherent and well-positioned for digital platform leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project descriptions; consolidate overlapping content to improve scannability and avoid dilution.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities—for example, traffic growth, engagement improvements, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption metrics from redesigns, analytics, and AI search work.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; punctuation/bullet formatting is inconsistent; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically unusual unless intentional branding. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/relevance: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger outcome-oriented phrasing like “modernizing enterprise platforms” or “leading digital transformation.”
- Reduce list length in sentence two; group related areas for smoother flow: web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search/UX.
- Consider adding one concrete scope marker from recent experience if space allows, e.g., “high-volume” could become “enterprise, high-traffic” or reference multi-publisher environments.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search and discovery” would be more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes multiple skills sections; simplify to avoid repetition.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the target roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure.”
- Replace broader items with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “operations”; “Workflow automation and platform integrations” for consistency.
- Consider a more focused version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Keep “AI-enabled search” and “public-sector advocacy” because they differentiate the profile.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “editorial systems,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills; this section should stay higher-level and more selective.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more impactful as a footer.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed X to achieve Y,” and replace vague phrases like “continued campaign growth” with a clearer benefit.
- Standardize style and punctuation: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent serial commas.
- Where possible, add scope or outcome signals without duplicating metrics already used elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo consulting and prior NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider keeping that and trimming the more repetitive entries.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and AI-enabled web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 4 focused impact bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations-improvement bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/microsites launched, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search success/engagement lift, stakeholder teams supported.
- Use stronger consultant phrasing: “Designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “advised leadership on,” instead of “consult,” “build,” “develop.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and “campaign/storytelling experiences” duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for the footer.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize new consulting scope and post-director contributions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 impact bullets, prioritizing the website migration, analytics buildout, and studio launch.
- Add outcome language where possible: adoption, efficiency gains, reporting speed, production savings, engagement growth, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Suggested phrasing:
- Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making.
- Launched NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding advocacy, event, and recurring multimedia production capacity.
- Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to strengthen operational consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep channel management here high-level.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears in the current consulting role; differentiate by emphasizing enterprise leadership and scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing execution scope, cross-functional coordination, and any measurable channel growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcomes where possible: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or workflow efficiency gains.
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-impact points, e.g. editorial planning across teams, weekly advocacy video production, and workflow/process improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier “Digital Media Manager / Producer” role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/operationalizing the series.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this version focused on execution rather than governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads broad rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and the most current, high-value strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “web modernization,” which better reflects recent senior roles.
- Keep terms parallel in structure; avoid mixing leadership, messaging, and planning language styles.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web modernization” to align with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration and current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates Core Competencies: “Digital governance & editorial systems.”
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is very close to Core Competencies: “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they matter for target roles; otherwise trim to avoid diluting recent enterprise Drupal work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with a clearer outcome-oriented phrase like “Airtable-based workflow systems” or “operational workflow systems.”
- If space allows, use “enterprise web platforms” or “digital platform implementation” to signal leadership, not just hands-on tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep here only if shortened.
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS/jQuery are already covered in “Technical + IT.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets for each tool.
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing terms: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “SEO and digital performance analysis,” “insight-driven optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive reporting dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis • Insight-driven optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep tools there and make this section more strategic.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive reporting dashboards” and better matches seniority.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior, outcome-oriented, and aligned to recent leadership in studio buildout and event production.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize scope: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Replace generic bullets with tighter, higher-level phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio operations and production workflows
- PTZ camera systems and multi-camera setups
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: **Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming and recurring event content**
- Keep wording consistent with leadership level; avoid sounding purely hands-on/technical.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” already appears in Core Competencies; use this section to add specificity, not repeat the same terms.
- Tool-level detail is already covered under “Multimedia & Creative Tools,” so avoid listing software here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal is the lead platform; consider bolding Drupal if formatting allows.
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without repeating experience bullets, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space is tight, drop **GitHub Pages** unless it is materially important to target roles; it reads less strategic than the others.
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list broader and this one more tool-specific.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this section should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: APIs, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add level/scope instead of just tools, e.g. “used for CMS customization, campaign microsites, tagging, serverless scripts, and deployment workflows”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless important: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5 • CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere, so avoid repeating it if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to group by function and highlight stronger tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it feels older/less relevant than the rest.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the leadership narrative.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of a pure list, e.g. “Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning and cross-team coordination using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack and Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement systems leadership. Since email operations already appear in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade platforms over basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rephrase to signal category and scale: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses rather than more tools: **(campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first; otherwise keep enterprise tools before Mailchimp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already covered repeatedly in recent work experience; avoid adding claims here unless they introduce distinct technical capability.
- “Engagement” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-focused, not strategic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and repeats analytics platforms already proven in the recent Director role. Tighten it to emphasize optimization capability, not just software names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • dashboard development • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Put the most strategic/recently evidenced tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with stronger phrasing like **dashboard development** or **executive reporting**; if true, consider **conversion analysis** instead of generic SEO

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already called out in the **Director of Digital Media** entry, so avoid repeating the exact same sequence elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and concrete so it reads as the foundation for the leadership roles that follow.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer delivery language: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house communications capacity.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the capability, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating “strengthening workflows” if later roles already cover operational improvement in more strategic terms.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation support plus first-of-its-kind multimedia execution.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting program and policy teams, while expanding NACo’s early digital storytelling efforts.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague wording like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with specifics if possible: web features, audio segments, interview production, or policy explainers.
- Add any measurable scope available: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team/enterprise-scale language for later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It should be tightened and framed to support the stronger, more recent leadership and studio-production experience elsewhere on the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Split tools from capabilities for clarity; e.g. “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio production • Podcast production”
- Use consistent naming: spell out Adobe products and replace “workflows” with a more direct capability like “studio production” or “live broadcast production.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value tool/system instead of generic phrasing (for example, streaming platform, switcher, or audio workflow tool) to make the list more concrete.
